compound.name: carvacrol
compound.one_liner: Thymol's positional isomer; the main phenol of Greek oregano oil (39.8 % cultivated; 23.3 % wild chemotype).

biosynthesis.pathway: MEP/terpenoid (plastidial; from geranyl diphosphate); aromatised by P450s + a short-chain dehydrogenase
biosynthesis.note: Formed from γ-terpinene by the same P450/dehydrogenase system as thymol [42].

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Thymus vulgaris L., Thymus zygis L., herba. EMA/HMPC/342334/2013 (12 Nov 2013). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-thymus-vulgaris-l-vulgaris-zygis-l-herba_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: EMA lists carvacrol among main components; Ph. Eur. thymol + carvacrol min. 40 % of oil. Kosakowska 2020 did not quantify carvacrol separately. | Basis as recorded: ppm as listed by Duke (basis not stated per row; for 'Essent. Oil' parts it is ppm of the oil, 10000 ppm = 1 %)

occurrences.plant_part: upper non-woody shoots at bloom onset
occurrences.source_citation: Kosakowska O, et al. (2021) Antioxidant and antibacterial activity of essential oils and hydroethanolic extracts of Greek oregano (O. vulgare L. subsp. hirtum (Link) Ietswaart) and common oregano (O. vulgare L. subsp. vulgare). Molecules 26(4):988
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke (Lagouri 1993): CARVACROL Shoot max 26865 ppm. KNApSAcK: C00000156. De Martino 2009 chemotype 1: carvacrol 23.34 %. Neither paper supports the 60-80 % figure in curation.md. | Basis as recorded: % of essential oil

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

compound.teaching_note: Oregano and thyme make the same two phenols in different ratios. Greek oregano is usually carvacrol-type, but thymol and linalool chemotypes exist [21, 22].
gaps: The '60-80 % of hirtum oil' figure is unsourced and was replaced by 39.8 % and 23.3 %.
No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
